DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Malignancy (likely Epithelial Ovarian Cancer with pseudomyxoma peritonei or mucinous variant)

Despite the normal CA125, the presence of a large right ovarian mass and significant ascites in a 40-year-old woman is highly suspicious for malignancy. Many epithelial ovarian cancers, particularly mucinous subtypes, do not always elevate CA125 levels. The shortness of breath is consistent with diaphragmatic elevation from the massive tumor burden and ascites. I recommend proceeding with a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to evaluate for peritoneal spread and metastatic disease.
